newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgargas cuts gas supplies to Bourgas oil refinery.
newsitem.headline: Bulgargas cuts gas supplies to Bourgas oil refinery.

text.p: Bulgarian state gas supplier Bulgargas said on Thursday it had cut off supplies of Russian natural gas to the country's biggest oil refinery Neftochim which has not paid its bills since last year.
A company statement said it had taken the measure following warnings from suppliers threatening to cut natural gas transfers to Bulgaria. Bulgargas has been having trouble meeting its own debts.
Since the beginning of this year, Neftochim has run up debts to Bulgargas of 14 billion levs, or $9 million at the current exchange rate, the statement said.

Neftochim owes another 4.5 billion levs for 1996, which were $15 million under the exchange rate at the end of the year, it said, adding that now the sum was only $3 million under the current rate and Bulgargas had lost $12 million.
Neftochim spokeswoman Tatyana Hadzhieva said it would be very difficult for the refinery to pay Bulgargas.
"We have replaced the gas with mazut (heavy fuel oil), which we have produced and it is very expensive for us to keep the production going," Hadzhieva told Reuters.
She said the plant had switched off three installations, including one ethylene plant, which would not affect production.

Neftochim owes millions of dollars to its crude suppliers and was forced to limit its sales last month due to a lack of cash to buy crude. The refinery's limited output provoked a severe fuel crisis, which eased earlier this month.
Bulgaria's interim government said recently it would sell a stake in Neftochim but did not specify how big the stake would be.

Russia's state oil holding company Rosneft, one of Neftochim's main suppliers whose takings from the refinery are worth some $100 million, said earlier this month it was interested in buying a majority stake in the refinery.
